class.name: VideoStreamPlayer
class.brief_description: A control used for video playback.
class.description: A control used for playback of [VideoStream] resources. Supported video formats are [url=https://www.theora.org/]Ogg Theora[/url] ([code].ogv[/code], [VideoStreamTheora]) and any format exposed via a GDExtension plugin. [b]Warning:[/b] On Web, video playback [i]will[/i] perform poorly due to missing architecture-specific assembly optimizations.

method.name: get_stream_metadata
method.description: Returns advisory metadata supplied by the native media backend. Fields include [code]title[/code] (at most 256 characters), [code]title_source[/code] ([code]youtube[/code], [code]container[/code], or [code]filename[/code]), [code]source[/code] (the original input), [code]source_type[/code], [code]duration[/code], [code]is_live[/code], and [code]opened[/code]. YouTube titles reuse existing URL resolution; direct media uses an embedded title tag or decoded filename, without a second title lookup. [code]opened = false[/code] denotes preliminary resolution metadata; successful readiness publishes [code]opened = true[/code]. Live DVR duration remains zero; use [method get_dvr_window] for the rewind range. The playback emits [code]metadata_changed(metadata)[/code] on the main thread. Native snapshots also include [code]playback_instance_id[/code] and [code]generation[/code]; superseded opens cannot emit stale metadata. Applications must additionally associate callbacks with their own queue-entry IDs, since URLs can repeat. Metadata never changes a resource name, playlist title, or user-entered evidence title. Preserve authoritative application titles and treat discovered titles as optional plain text. Unsupported backends return an empty dictionary.

method.name: get_dvr_window
method.description: Returns the native backend's observed DVR window. With YouTube DVR enabled on [VideoStreamMedia], the dictionary contains [code]available[/code], [code]start[/code], [code]end[/code], [code]live_position[/code], [code]position[/code], and [code]opened_position[/code] (the fixed target selected for the current opening) in seconds on the playback instance's fixed timeline. [code]timeline_origin_utc[/code], [code]start_utc[/code], [code]end_utc[/code], and [code]position_utc[/code] express the same timeline in Unix seconds. The safe live position leaves a few segments of buffering. Set [member stream_position] to rewind or seek forward; expired and future requests clamp to the actual available window. Range observations update when the decoder reloads its playlist and are refreshed on seeking. They can become stale while playback is paused or buffered far behind live. An unsupported backend returns an empty dictionary or [code]available = false[/code].

method.name: seek_to_live
method.description: Requests a fresh native YouTube DVR opening at the safe live edge. Returns [code]false[/code] if DVR is unavailable. The request is asynchronous, preserves pause state, and emits [code]seek_completed(position)[/code] on the playback instance after worker preparation. Superseded requests do not deliver stale completions.

method.name: get_stream_playback
method.description: Returns the current playback instance. On native Windows, Linux/BSD, and Android builds with the media streaming module, its readiness, buffering, error, and seek completion signals can be used to coordinate asynchronous media loading. This method is not exposed on Web.

method.name: get_stream_length
method.description: The length of the current stream, in seconds.

method.name: get_stream_name
method.description: Returns the video stream's name, or [code]"<No Stream>"[/code] if no video stream is assigned.

method.name: get_video_texture
method.description: Returns the current frame as a [Texture2D].

method.name: is_playing
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the video is playing. [b]Note:[/b] The video is still considered playing if paused during playback.

method.name: play
method.description: Starts the video playback from the beginning. If the video is paused, this will not unpause the video.

method.name: stop
method.description: Stops the video playback and sets the stream position to 0. [b]Note:[/b] Although the stream position will be set to 0, the first frame of the video stream won't become the current frame.

members.member: The embedded audio track to play.
If [code]true[/code], playback starts when the scene loads.
Amount of time in milliseconds to store in buffer while playing.
Audio bus to use for sound playback.
If [code]true[/code], the video scales to the control size. Otherwise, the control minimum size will be automatically adjusted to match the video stream's dimensions.
If [code]true[/code], the video restarts when it reaches its end.

The stream's current speed scale. [code]1.0[/code] is the normal speed, while [code]2.0[/code] is double speed and [code]0.5[/code] is half speed. A speed scale of [code]0.0[/code] pauses the video, similar to setting [member paused] to [code]true[/code].
The assigned video stream. See description for supported formats.
The current position of the stream, in seconds.
